**City Council Approves New Riverfront Park After Years of Planning**

RIVERTON — In a unanimous vote Tuesday night, the Riverton City Council approved final funding for a new 22-acre riverfront park, marking the culmination of a multi-year planning process shaped by public workshops and environmental reviews.

The project, officially titled Riverbend Commons, will include walking and cycling paths, a small outdoor performance lawn, native-plant landscaping, and improved river access for kayaks and community boating programs. Construction is scheduled to begin in late April, with the city targeting a phased opening starting this fall.

“This is an investment in public space that residents have asked for repeatedly,” Mayor Elena Cruz said following the vote. “We’re connecting neighborhoods to the river in a way that’s safe, accessible, and designed to last.”

Funding will come from a combination of municipal bonds, a state recreation grant, and private donations coordinated through the Riverton Parks Foundation. City engineers said early site work will focus on shoreline stabilization and drainage improvements to reduce flood impacts on nearby streets.

Public information sessions on construction timelines and detours are expected to be announced in the coming weeks.
